parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence exists (explicitly stated), consensual same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2014, and there is no documented targeting, universal-exposure measure, facility/custody rule, or violence record. Worst documented feature is tier 5: absent protections and open questions (border screening, wards, custody, care) — questions, not exposures. Positives are structural rather than demonstrated: penal-code reform, UN engagement, and 2019 head-of-state equality rhetoric signal a reform-oriented institutional culture, though no documented social acceptance, service enforcement, or remedy machinery appears. Silence in this thin dossier is not safety, so I do not credit unstated acceptance; but neither does the record support a tier 1–3 deduction. No sexuality statute remains to weigh. Absent documented friction or hostility, and absent any verified protection, the middle-upper reduced-risk zone fits.
